expect.note: every specs/decisions/ADR-*.md carries a **Ruling**: block of at most 3 lines before its first `---`, specs/decisions/INDEX.md lists each ADR number exactly once, and every ADR reference — canonical `ADR-0NN` or an identifier spelling like `adr019` — in README.md, CLAUDE.md, tasks/TODO.md, tasks/DONE.md and under src/, evals/, specs/, .github/, docs/ and prompts/ resolves: the decision exists, and a sectioned citation names a section that ADR has

provenance: The decision-first ADR convention adds a mandatory compressed header (Ruling/Because/Enforced by) to every ADR plus a one-line-per-ADR index, so a reader who wants 'what are the current rules' does not have to read the incident narrative behind each one. Nothing enforced the header's shape or the index's completeness once written by hand, so both were free to rot the next time an ADR is added or an existing one is edited. Watched red twice while building this case: once with the header stripped from ADR-003 down to just a bare '**Ruling**:' line followed by 4 lines of prose before '**Because**:' (missing_ruling/ruling_too_long both empty, ruling_too_long: [{'file': 'ADR-003-m3-recovery-thresholds.md', 'lines': 4}]), and once with the ADR-006 line deleted from INDEX.md (missing_from_index: ['006']). T-R52 (PR #35 cold review) added the citation half: specs/decisions/INDEX.md, evals/run.py (twice) and .github/workflows/eval.yml all attributed the one-variable-per-suite wall-clock override to the M36 judge decision, number 017, when the ruling is ADR-019 §4 — and INDEX's ADR-002 line also listed 017 among the ADRs amending it, which it does not. Nothing read a citation body, so this case graded the header convention beside four wrong numbers for a whole milestone. What is graded now is what a machine can settle: the decision exists, and where the citation names a section in the `§N` form this repo already uses, that section exists. The judge decision has no numbered sections at all, so that miscitation is red the moment it is written in the sectioned form. Watched red twice, and the mutations are described rather than quoted here, because a literal miscitation in this file would be swept by the check it documents (the same reason REPORT_CITATION_SKIP spells its one exception out in prose): (1) the workflow's repaired citation rewritten back to the judge decision with its §4 intact -> {cites_no_such_section: [{file: '.github/workflows/eval.yml', cites: <that decision, §4>, has_sections: []}]}; (2) a README reference to decision number 042, which no file carries -> {cites_no_such_adr: [{file: 'README.md', cites: <that number>}]}. Every citation in that set resolves on the committed tree; the count is not published here, because it moves with every edit and nothing grades it (PR #36 R13). tasks/reviews/ is deliberately out of scope: those are verbatim reviewer records the repo does not edit, and six of PR #29's own citations point the judge ADR's number at wall-clock sections it has never had — the record of the confusion T-R52 repaired. PR #36 R3/R4 widened it twice, each watched red. The scope: all of `tasks/` and CLAUDE.md were excluded while the comment and this provenance said only the verbatim reviewer records were — ~100 hand-edited citations ungraded. tasks/TODO.md, tasks/DONE.md and CLAUDE.md are in now; pointing TODO.md's citations at a decision number no file carries gives {cites_no_such_adr: [{file: 'tasks/TODO.md', cites: <that number>}, ...]}. The spelling: the resolver read only the canonical form, so a fifth T-R52 miscitation sat inside a JSON key naming the judge decision for mutations of the per-suite override (ADR-019 §4) — invisible while this case reported every citation resolving. The key is renamed and the resolver reads identifier spellings; the same key pointed at a nonexistent decision gives {cites_no_such_adr: [{file: 'evals/adversarial/fast-wall-clock-budget.json', cites: <that number>}]}. Extended 2026-08-28 with `title_number_is_not_the_filename`, the conjunct that closes T-M41-5, T-M42-7 and M45-D2 — three separately-logged blocks that are one defect, which is itself the finding: `specs/decisions/ADR-022-m40-declaring-a-domain-from-live-runs.md` opened `# ADR-020:` while `ADR-020-m32-observation-drill-down.md` opened the same way, so two files claimed 020 by title and one of them is cited as 022 by INDEX.md, the support matrix and ADR-024/025/028. It survived three separate spec-drift audits because every existing conjunct here keys on the FILENAME or on INDEX.md and none compared a file's H1 to its own name. M41 nearly attributed a rule to ADR-022 that ADR-022 does not contain. Watched RED against the tree as it stood: `{title_number_is_not_the_filename: [{file: ADR-022-...md, title_says: ADR-020}]}` — the live defect, not a planted one.

triage.note: same shape as support-matrix-cites-real-cases and opt-in-expect-keys-declared: this guards a documentation contract, not the product, so it stays pure code with no network and no browser. It checks the header EXISTS and is short, and that INDEX.md's coverage is complete and non-duplicated — it does not grade whether a Ruling sentence is an honest compression of the ADR's Decision section, which is a human judgment act the same way declaring a support-matrix status is. The citation half stops at resolution: it does not grade that the cited section RULES on the subject of the citing sentence. Three mechanisms for that were measured against this tree and all three were unusable as a gate -- rare-word overlap between the citing line and the Ruling (70 false positives), the cited ADR having to enforce a mechanism named on the same line (40), and a file having to cite every ADR that uniquely owns an identifier it uses (8 files, every one of them legitimate). Logged as T-R57 rather than shipped as noise.
